title: 3D quantification of autophagy activation and autophagosome-to-mitochondria recruitment in a Drosophila model of Parkinson’s disease
protocol: Collect female and/or male flies from fly cross expressing mito-GFP, mCherry-Atg8a, and the desired GAL4 driver.
Maintain collected flies in standard food vials, transferring to new food vials two times per week until flies reach desired age.
Anesthetize aged experimental flies on a CO2 pad one at a time.
Pick up an anesthetized fly with dissecting forceps and place it on a dissecting plate near a droplet of 0.3% PBT.
Decapitate the fly quickly using forceps and place the head into the droplet.
Dissect the brain under a dissecting microscope by removing eye discs and cuticle.
Place the dissected brains in a glass spot plate well containing 3.7% formaldehyde for 15 minutes.
Transfer the fixed brain from fixing solution to another well containing 0.3% PBT using forceps.
Up to five brains of the same genotype can be transferred to a single well.
Place the glass well plate on an orbital shaker for 5 minutes.
Discard used solution using a fine tip transfer pipette.
Add fresh 0.3% PBT to wells.
Repeat washing step four times.
Ensure brains are in solution before placing the plate on the shaker.
Remove 0.3% PBT from each well under the dissecting microscope.
Add 500 μL blocking solution to brain-containing wells.
Keep the glass spot plate on the orbital shaker for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare a fresh primary antibody solution (1:100 anti-tyrosine hydroxylase).
Place 10 μL of the primary antibody solution in each microtiter well.
Transfer brains from glass wells to antibody-containing microtiter wells using forceps.
Store the microtiter plate in an empty pipette box with a moist towel at 4°C overnight.
Using forceps, transfer the brains from the microtiter plate to a glass well containing 0.3% PBT.
Wash the brains in 0.3% PBT four times for 5 min on the orbital shaker using a fine tip transfer pipette.
Remove 0.3% PBT and add 500 μL of blocking solution.
Place the brains on a shaker for at least 30 min.
Prepare a 1:200 solution of Alexa Fluor® 405-conjugated secondary antibody to blocking solution.
Remove blocking solution and add 400 μL of secondary antibody solution to each well.
Protect from light and place the brains on an orbital shaker for 2 h.
Replace secondary antibody solution with 0.3% PBT and incubate for five minutes on a shaker.
Repeat washing procedure four times.
Label a microscope slide with genotype, antibody label, fly age, treatment, and date.
Place a small drop of 70% glycerol onto the slide near the frosted left side.
Drag the glycerol droplet to the right along the slide with the transfer pipette.
Use forceps to remove one brain at a time from the final wash and place it in the left region of the glycerol line.
Carefully drag the brain to the right, maintaining orientation for ease of imaging.
Align brains in the glycerol line.
Remove excess glycerol from the slide using a Kim Wipe®.
Re-orient displaced brains.
Place a small horizontal line of Prolong Antifade® above the line of brains.
Carefully place a coverslip over the top of the mounted brains.
Allow the mounting media to spread for 1 to 2 min, avoiding light exposure.
Seal the coverslip to the slide with clear nail polish.
Using a marker, draw a line indicating the location of the brains so they can be easily located during imaging.
Place slide in a slide box and store at −20°C.
Turn on computer, confocal microscope and open LASX application.
Turn on the 488 nm and 532 nm excitation lasers.
Set pinhole to 1 AU.
Set the image resolution to 512 × 512 pixels and speed to 600 Hz for fast scanning while locating volume of interest (VOI) boundaries.
Using the 63× oil objective, locate the brain and the region of interest (ROI) on the confocal microscope.
Use the setting for Sequence 3 if the brains have been immunostained.
If not using immunostaining, locate the ROI as rapidly as possible using the fluorescence of GFP or mCherry.
Manually manipulate the z position around your VOI by clicking the “Live” button in the LASX application.
At the top of the VOI, click the “Begin” button.
Move the stage to the bottom of the VOI and click the “End” button.
Change the pixels per image and image capture speed to 1024 × 1024 and 400 Hz, respectively.
Set the z-stack step to 340 nm.
Select “Between Lines” under the “Sequential Scan” tab.
Click “Start” to take the image.
Save the image in “lif” format with a descriptive title.
Open Image-Pro Premier 3D Application and open lif files.
Under the “3D View” tab, click the “Reload” button.
Uncheck “Auto” under the “Load Image” window.
Click “Reset” to change all values to 1.
Under the “3D View” tab, click the “Show VOI” icon.
Under the “3D View” tab, click the “Show VOI handles” icon.
Adjust the volume of interest (VOI) using the arrow tool from the “3D View” panel.
Add volume:volume settings with a minimum volume of 0.01 and maximum volume of 1.5 μm.
Click the “Ranges” button to turn it on.
Click the “Add Iso-Surface” icon in the right panel.
Select channel 2 (532 nm, sequence 2 during image capture) from the drop-down menu.
Uncheck “Auto” and click “Reset” to change all values to 1.
Select “Lo-Pass 3×3×3” from the “Filter” drop-down menu.
Select “Auto Bright” from the “Threshold type” drop-down menu.
Under “Volume Surface Channel 2,” click the “Count” button to select puncta that fit volume and threshold criteria.
Adjust minimum “Volume Surface Channel 2” intensity range to collect visible puncta.
Click data table under the 3D Measure tab.
Optional: If collecting data in immunolabeled cells, manually remove puncta outside of labeled regions.
In the “3D View” tab, select the arrow tool and click on each unwanted object then press delete.
Under the “3D Measure” tab, click “Data Table,” then click on Microsoft Excel icon to export the data to an Excel spreadsheet.
Click on the disk icon to save this isosurface file representing autophagosomes.
Delete channel 2 isosurface from the viewing window.
If visible puncta fall out of detection range, repeat steps adjusting minimum “Volume Surface Channel” range in step to collect visible puncta.
Manually remove puncta that have already been exported to Excel.
Click “Types” on 3D Measure tab and add, “Coloc Pearson.”
Click on “Add 3D Colocalization” isosurface.
Select the “channel red, channel green” option from the drop-down menu.
Click “Reset,” and enter “1” for each pixel dimension.
Select “Lo-Pass 3×3×3” filter.
Select “Auto Bright.”
Check box for close edges.
Set the threshold for the red channel using same minimum threshold for red isosurface in step 48 for each saved isosurface.
Click folder icon under colocalization and open the saved isosurface file.
Manually remove identified objects that have Pearson’s correlation coefficients less than or equal to zero from data table.
Export data to Excel.
Repeat steps for each saved isosurface.
Count the number of colocalization measurements.
